Notes: CDIAL 10286 mṛttikā gives Kumauni māṭo/māṭi and Nepali māṭo, eastern māṭi earth/clay. Dotyali məṭi retains the retroflex and final i with a central first vowel; this soil response belongs with the earth family. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: məṭi. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

CDIAL 6261 *dādda explicitly gives Nepali dājyu elder brother. Dotyali dāju fits with loss of the palatal glide; the source length is preserved. This is a nursery kinship family. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: dāju. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

CDIAL 10055 māma gives Nepali/Hindi māmā and Prakrit māma mother’s brother. Kochila Tharu məmə fits with central vowels. The elicited seniority is contextual and is not reconstructed for the ancestor; the dictionary identifies a nursery formation. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: məmə. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

CDIAL 4560 cakṣus gives Bengali cok(h)/cauk eye and Prakrit cakkhu. Bengali tʃok is the corresponding affricate transcription. Turner marks the eastern forms probably borrowed from Prakrit, so this family link retains that historical qualification. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: tʃok. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

CDIAL 986 asmad gives Prakrit amhe and Hindi/Bhojpuri ham, Gujarati ame we. Bhili hamũ fits the plural-pronoun family with final nasal vowel retained; exclusivity is an elicited local distinction, not a reconstructed property of asmad. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: hamũ. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

CDIAL 12459.1 śilā gives Oriya siḷa stone/grinding stone, Bengali sil and Assamese xil. Adivasi Oriya sil stone fits the single-l branch, retaining final-vowel loss; the doubled *śillā subsection is not selected. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: sil. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.

CDIAL 9459 bhāra gives Punjabi/Lahnda bhārā heavy and western Pahari bhārā. Dogri pārə fits the regional devoiced onset and final schwa alongside those adjective forms. The onset comparison is regional, not an assertion that Turner quotes this exact Dogri response. Local Indo-Aryan transmission remains unresolved. Exact response: pārə. Joint SIL review 2026-09-14.
